description.en: Palestine, Lebanon, southern Syria and Transjordan, plus Sinai as part of Ottoman Egypt (from Jan 1517); control east of the Jordan and in the desert margins was loose.
description.ar: فلسطين ولبنان وجنوب سوريا وشرق الأردن، إضافة إلى سيناء بوصفها جزءًا من مصر العثمانية (منذ كانون الثاني/يناير 1517)؛ وكانت السيطرة شرق الأردن وفي أطراف الصحراء رخوة.
description.he: פלשתינה, לבנון, דרום סוריה ועבר הירדן, בתוספת סיני כחלק ממצרים העות׳מאנית (מינואר 1517); השליטה ממזרח לירדן ובשולי המדבר הייתה רופפת.

sources.quote: Selim defeated the Mamluk armies at the battles of Marj Dābiq (north of Aleppo; August 24, 1516) and Raydāniyyah (near Cairo; January 22, 1517), thus bringing Syria, Egypt, and Palestine under Ottoman rule.
on August 24, 1516, when the Ottoman sultan Selim I routed the Mamluk armies at the Battle of Marj Dābiq. Palestine began its four centuries under Ottoman domination.
From 1516 to 1918 Acre was, except for brief intervals, under the rule of the Ottoman Turks.
Ottoman control in the 18th century was indirect.
After Marj Dabiq, Selim I's army advanced southward, and Syria passed quickly into the possession of the Ottomans, whose advent was in many places welcomed as meaning deliverance from the Mamluks.
came the bad news that the army that had gone to Gaza had suffered defeat on Sunday, the 24th, of Dhu'l Ka'dah.
In reality, the Damascus governors had only a tenuous hold over Jabal Nablus
Rather, it was the rulers of Acre—Zahir al-Umar (d. 1775), Ahmad Pasha al-Jazzar (d. 1804), Sulayman Pasha al-Adil (d. 1819), and Abdullah Pasha
Then, in 1831, all of Greater Syria fell under the rule of Muhammad Ali Pasha of Egypt

notes.en: Indirect control in the 18th century; autonomous rulers in Galilee/Acre (see zahir-al-umar-galilee, jazzar-acre).
notes.ar: سيطرة غير مباشرة في القرن 18؛ حكام شبه مستقلون في الجليل/عكا (انظر zahir-al-umar-galilee, jazzar-acre).
notes.he: שליטה עקיפה במאה ה-18; שליטים אוטונומיים בגליל/עכו (ראו zahir-al-umar-galilee, jazzar-acre).

description.en: Restored direct Ottoman rule after the Egyptian withdrawal; Tanzimat-era provinces. Karak and southern Transjordan administered from the 1890s; the Negev down to Aqaba under Jerusalem after the 1906 Ottoman-British boundary agreement (line from Rafah to the Gulf of Aqaba).
description.ar: استُعيد الحكم العثماني المباشر بعد الانسحاب المصري؛ ولايات عهد التنظيمات. أُديرت الكرك وجنوب شرق الأردن منذ تسعينيات القرن التاسع عشر؛ والنقب حتى العقبة تحت القدس بعد اتفاق الحدود العثماني-البريطاني 1906 (خط من رفح إلى خليج العقبة).
description.he: שלטון עות׳מאני ישיר הוחזר לאחר הנסיגה המצרית; מחוזות תקופת הטנזימאת. כרך ודרום עבר הירדן נוהלו משנות ה-90 של המאה ה-19; הנגב עד עקבה תחת ירושלים לאחר הסכם הגבול העות׳מאני-בריטי של 1906 (קו מרפיח למפרץ עקבה).

sources.locator: section 'Administrative Reorganization in the Aftermath of Egyptian Withdrawal'
sources.quote: After the withdrawal of Muhammad Ali's army back to Egypt at the end of 1840
When in 1840 the British, the Austrians, and the Russians came to the aid of the Ottomans, the Egyptians were forced to withdraw, and Palestine reverted to the Ottoman Empire.
In 1840 Al-Karak was occupied by Ibrahim Pasha; it was administered by the Ottomans in the 1890s
Consequently, the authority of the governor of Jerusalem extended to Aqaba—an area that included the entire Negev down to Aqaba.
In 1841 he and his family were granted the hereditary right to rule Egypt and the Sudan, but his power was still subjected to restraints, and the sultan’s suzerain rights remained intact.

sources.locator: ch. XVII, Admiral Stopford's dispatch dated 4 November 1840, p. 220
sources.quote: the town and fortress of Acre were taken possession of by the allied forces under my command this morning in the name of the Sultan.
The judge had thus been nominated by the central Ottoman government in Istanbul one year before the restoration of Ottoman rule in Jerusalem in November 1840.
in 1841, the Sultan conferred upon Mohammed Ali the hereditary Pashalik of Egypt, creating thereby, within boundaries defined by the Sultan, a privileged vassal State within the Empire.
Previous to 1894 this sanjaq was called Ma‘an and had its capital at Ma‘an. In 1894 Salt was added to the sanjaq and the capital was moved to Kerak.

sources.locator: Part I, history section on the British occupation, p. 24
sources.quote: at noon of the 9th December a Turkish parlementaire conveyed the surrender of the city to the Commander-in-Chief
on November 6, 1840, a letter from Muhammad Rüstem, the military governor of Damascus, announced that Ahmad Agha al-Dazdar was the interim mutasallim

notes.en: Sinai excluded: administered with Egypt, under the hereditary rule of Muhammad Ali's family (Ottoman suzerainty) after 1841.
notes.ar: سيناء مستثناة: كانت تُدار مع مصر، في ظل حكم أسرة محمد علي الوراثي (سيادة عثمانية) بعد 1841.
notes.he: סיני אינה כלולה: נוהלה עם מצרים, תחת שלטונה התורשתי של משפחת מוחמד עלי (ריבונות עות'מאנית) אחרי 1841.

description.en: After the capture of Jerusalem (Dec 1917) Ottoman forces still held northern Palestine, Transjordan, Lebanon and Syria; 'The remaining area was occupied by the British by October 1918.'
description.ar: بعد الاستيلاء على القدس (كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1917) ظلت القوات العثمانية تحتفظ بشمال فلسطين وشرق الأردن ولبنان وسوريا؛ 'The remaining area was occupied by the British by October 1918.' [احتل البريطانيون المنطقة المتبقية بحلول تشرين الأول/أكتوبر 1918].
description.he: לאחר כיבוש ירושלים (דצמבר 1917) עדיין החזיקו הכוחות העות׳מאניים בצפון פלשתינה, בעבר הירדן, בלבנון ובסוריה; “The remaining area was occupied by the British by October 1918.” [האזור שנותר נכבש בידי הבריטים עד אוקטובר 1918].

sources.locator: section 'World War I and after', paragraph 2
sources.quote: Jerusalem was captured by British and Allied forces under the command of General Sir Edmund (later 1st Viscount) Allenby in December 1917. The remaining area was occupied by the British by October 1918.

sources.locator: Part I, history section on the British occupation, p. 24
sources.quote: at noon of the 9th December a Turkish parlementaire conveyed the surrender of the city to the Commander-in-Chief

sources.locator: Part I, history section on the British occupation, p. 28
sources.quote: The part of Palestine already occupied was divided into the following districts: Jerusalem, Jaffa, Gaza, Hebron and Beersheba. This division continued in vigour until Lord Allenby’s great drive in September, 1918

sources.locator: Part I, history section on the British occupation, p. 28
sources.quote: when the remainder of Palestine, Syria and Cilicia were cleared of the Turks. Thereupon Military Governors were posted to Nablus, Jenin, Tulkeram, Haifa, Nazareth, Acre, Tiberias, and Safed.

sources.locator: ch. 7, section 'The End of the Empire and Turkish-Arab Relations'
sources.quote: With the occupation of Damascus and the rest of Syria by the Anglo-Arab forces in October 1918 and the Ottoman surrender at the Mudros cease-fire at the end of that month

sources.locator: Part I, ch. on the Mandate
sources.quote: Although formally still part of the Ottoman Empire, Palestine was under British military occupation since December 1917.
The battle of Megiddo occurred in Palestine between 19 and 25 September 1918.
The remaining area was occupied by the British by October 1918.
by October 1918 Amman and Damascus were in Allied hands
An Arab military force occupied Damascus in September 1918

notes.en: The front line of Dec 1917 - Sept 1918 is not mapped precisely. Britannica's Faisal I biography places the Arab occupation of Damascus in September 1918, its Jordan article says 'by October 1918'; the end month is given as October 1918 (Armistice of Mudros, 30 Oct 1918).
notes.ar: لم يُرسم خط الجبهة من كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1917 إلى أيلول/سبتمبر 1918 بدقة. تضع سيرة فيصل الأول في بريتانيكا الاحتلال العربي لدمشق في أيلول/سبتمبر 1918، وتقول مقالتها عن الأردن 'by October 1918'؛ وشهر النهاية معطى بأنه تشرين الأول/أكتوبر 1918 (هدنة مودروس، 30 تشرين الأول/أكتوبر 1918).
notes.he: קו החזית מדצמבר 1917 עד ספטמבר 1918 אינו ממופה בדיוק. הביוגרפיה של פייסל הראשון בבריטניקה ממקמת את הכיבוש הערבי של דמשק בספטמבר 1918, והמאמר שלה על ירדן אומר 'by October 1918'; חודש הסיום ניתן כאוקטובר 1918 (שביתת הנשק של מודרוס, 30 באוקטובר 1918).

description.en: Ottoman-held part of the map area in 1917 before the Gaza-Beersheba line broke: Palestine north of that line, plus Transjordan (Aqaba was taken by Faisal's Arab army in July 1917), the Golan, Syria and Lebanon.
description.ar: الجزء الذي كان بيد العثمانيين من منطقة الخريطة عام 1917 قبل انكسار خط غزة–بئر السبع: فلسطين شمال ذلك الخط، إضافة إلى شرق الأردن (أخذ جيش فيصل العربي العقبة في تموز/يوليو 1917) والجولان وسوريا ولبنان.
description.he: החלק מאזור המפה שהיה בידי העות׳מאנים ב-1917 לפני פריצת קו עזה–באר שבע: פלשתינה מצפון לקו זה, בתוספת עבר הירדן (עקבה נלקחה בידי הצבא הערבי של פייסל ביולי 1917), הגולן, סוריה ולבנון.

sources.quote: The British 20 Corps launched an attack on Beersheba at dawn on 31 October 1917.
In July 1917 the army of Prince Faisal ibn Hussein ... captured Al-ʿAqabah

notes.en: Exact front lines not reconstructed; partial units are schematic. AWM: 'On 6 November, after severe fighting, Turkish forces began to withdraw from Gaza'.
notes.ar: لم تُعاد بناء خطوط الجبهة الدقيقة؛ والوحدات الجزئية تخطيطية. AWM: 'On 6 November, after severe fighting, Turkish forces began to withdraw from Gaza'.
notes.he: קווי החזית המדויקים לא שוחזרו; היחידות החלקיות סכמטיות. AWM: 'On 6 November, after severe fighting, Turkish forces began to withdraw from Gaza'.

description.en: Ottoman occupation of much of the Sinai peninsula in the First World War: posts at El-Arish and Qal'at al-Nakhl from late 1914, the two attacks on the Suez Canal (February 1915; July-August 1916), and withdrawal after the defeats at Romani, Magdhaba and Rafa (August 1916 - January 1917).
description.ar: الاحتلال العثماني لمعظم شبه جزيرة سيناء في الحرب العالمية الأولى: مواقع في العريش وقلعة النخل منذ أواخر 1914، والهجومان على قناة السويس (شباط/فبراير 1915؛ تموز/يوليو - آب/أغسطس 1916)، والانسحاب بعد الهزائم في رمانة والمغضبة ورفح (آب/أغسطس 1916 - كانون الثاني/يناير 1917).
description.he: הכיבוש העות'מאני של רוב חצי האי סיני במלחמת העולם הראשונה: מוצבים באל-עריש ובקלעת א-נח'ל מסוף 1914, שתי ההתקפות על תעלת סואץ (פברואר 1915; יולי-אוגוסט 1916), והנסיגה אחרי התבוסות ברומאני, במגדבה וברפיח (אוגוסט 1916 - ינואר 1917).

sources.quote: the three years (December, 1914, to December, 1917) which I spent in Syria
The detachment of Beduin volunteers under the command of Major Muntaz Bey had seized El-Arish and fortified itself there.
had occupied the Kalaat-ul-Nahl in the centre of the Sinai Desert.
In early 1915, Great Britain withdrew its forces towards the Suez Canal and Turkey occupied much of the Sinai, remaining there until El Arish was taken in December 1916.
Osmanlı Ordusu 14 Ocak 1915’ten itibaren gece yürüyüşleriyle Bi’rüssebi‘den Süveyş Kanalı’na doğru yöneldi.
The Turkish forces launched their first attack on the Suez Canal, Britain's vital link to the East and Australia, on 3 February 1915
Bahriye Nâzırı Cemal Paşa kumandasındaki Türk kuvvetleri 3 Şubat’ta kanalı geçmeye giriştiler; fakat başarısızlığa uğrayarak 15 Şubat’ta geldikleri yere döndüler.
After this attack the British forces pushed their defences out 10 km east of the canal.
compelled it to withdraw to El Arish. Ultimately the force had to evacuate El Arish itself
sources.note: Djemal dates the evacuation to 'December i6th' [16th] 1916 in the OCR text; the British entered El Arish later that month.

sources.quote: The defences around Magdhaba were captured on 23 December, and those at Rafa on 9 January 1917.
The last small garrisons of Turkish forces were defeated in February 1917, completing the Allied occupation of the Sinai peninsula

notes.en: Start: El-Arish and Qal'at al-Nakhl were already held by Ottoman volunteer detachments when Djemal Pasha reached Syria in December 1914 (Djemal); the Taba award dates the occupation of 'much of the Sinai' to early 1915, after Britain withdrew towards the canal. The main army that attacked the canal on 3 February 1915 returned to its base in mid-February (TDV), but Ottoman posts stayed in the peninsula. End: El-Arish was evacuated in December 1916 (Djemal; Taba), Magdhaba and Rafa fell on 23 December 1916 and 9 January 1917, and the last small garrisons were defeated in February 1917 (AWM). The British-held canal zone and the moving front of 1916 are not modelled; the egypt-1 slice (sinai-egypt, from December 1914) overlaps this one and could be made partial for these years.
notes.ar: البداية: كانت العريش وقلعة النخل في يد مفارز عثمانية من المتطوعين حين وصل جمال باشا إلى سوريا في كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1914 (جمال)؛ ويؤرخ حكم طابا احتلال 'معظم سيناء' بأوائل 1915 بعد انسحاب بريطانيا نحو القناة. وعاد الجيش الرئيسي الذي هاجم القناة في 3 شباط/فبراير 1915 إلى قاعدته في منتصف شباط (TDV)، لكن المواقع العثمانية بقيت في شبه الجزيرة. النهاية: أُخليت العريش في كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1916 (جمال؛ طابا)، وسقطت المغضبة ورفح في 23 كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1916 و9 كانون الثاني/يناير 1917، وهُزمت آخر الحاميات الصغيرة في شباط/فبراير 1917 (AWM). ولا تُمثَّل منطقة القناة التي احتفظت بها بريطانيا ولا تحركات الجبهة عام 1916؛ وتتداخل شريحة egypt-1 (sinai-egypt منذ كانون الأول/ديسمبر 1914) مع هذه الشريحة ويمكن جعلها جزئية لهذه السنوات.
notes.he: התחלה: אל-עריש וקלעת א-נח'ל כבר הוחזקו בידי יחידות מתנדבים עות'מאניות כשג'מאל פאשה הגיע לסוריה בדצמבר 1914 (ג'מאל); פסק הבוררות בטאבה מתארך את כיבוש 'רוב סיני' לראשית 1915, אחרי שבריטניה נסוגה לעבר התעלה. הצבא העיקרי שתקף את התעלה ב-3 בפברואר 1915 חזר לבסיסו באמצע פברואר (TDV), אך מוצבים עות'מאניים נשארו בחצי האי. סיום: אל-עריש פונתה בדצמבר 1916 (ג'מאל; טאבה), מגדבה ורפיח נפלו ב-23 בדצמבר 1916 וב-9 בינואר 1917, וחילות המצב הקטנים האחרונים הובסו בפברואר 1917 (AWM). אזור התעלה שבידי בריטניה והחזית הנעה של 1916 אינם ממודלים; הפרוסה egypt-1 (sinai-egypt, מדצמבר 1914) חופפת לזו ואפשר להפוך אותה לחלקית בשנים אלה.
